`tateChainStructMap` (diagonal via `t_id`; far via initiality of the empty overlap; adjacent via
`hf` / `hb`).

  (hf :
    ∀ (i j : ULift.{u, 0} ℤ),

        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (annulusOverlapChart R I q) (k i) =
          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (annulusChartTransitionSpf R I q hI).hom

          CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (annulusChartTransitionSpf R I q hI).inv
            (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (annulusOverlapChart R I q) (k j)))
  (i j : ULift.{u, 0} ℤ) :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp

**`a + b` is invertible modulo `J·S` as soon as `a` is invertible in `S` and `a · b ∈ J`.**

Geometrically: in the formal spectrum `Spf (S, J·S)` the basic opens `D(a)` and `D(b)` are
disjoint, because `a · b` dies in the residue ring; so on `D(a)` the element `b` vanishes and
`a + b` agrees with the unit `a`. This is the hypothesis `adicAwayTransEquiv'` consumes, and at the
Tate annulus it is the whole geometric content of the splitting: `x · y = q` lies in the ideal of
definition.

**The stalk maps of the glued Tate diagonal are surjective** (source-local half of the
closed-immersion criterion for the diagonal, EGA I §10.15). Being surjective on stalks is a
condition local on the source, so by joint surjectivity of the two open-immersion charts
`(tateCurveFormalGlueData …).ι b` it suffices to check it after precomposing with each `ι b`. On
the `b`-chart the diagonal factors as the affine diagonal `diagChart` followed by the open-immersion
chart `ι ⟨(b, b)⟩` of the self-product. The two chart stalk maps are isomorphisms, and `diagChart`
has surjective stalk maps: its underlying `presheafedSpaceMap` is the topology-free formal spectrum
of the surjective codiagonal `∇`, whose stalk maps are surjective by
`isClosedEmbedding_base_and_surjective_stalkMap_of_surjective`, with target ideal identified through
`map_codiagonal_eq` and `annulus_map_eq`. Composing (surjective after cancelling the chart
isomorphisms) gives the claim.

relation and the self-inverse property of the chart-swap transition.

      (CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.desc (annulusOverlapChart R I q) (annulusOverlapChartY R I q))
      (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (AlgebraicGeometry.diagChart R I q hI)
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.tateSelfProductFormalGlueDataInv R I q hq hI).ι

          CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.inl))

doc:
**Diagonal-chart transition reconciliation.** Through the affine diagonals, the annulus chart
transition `annulusChartTransitionSpf` realises the diagonal both-summand transition
`bothSummandDiag`. The proof reduces (via `codiagonal_naturality` and the clean `lrsMap`-form
`annulusChartTransitionSpf_hom_eq`) to the bridge identity
`annulusFibreChartTransitionAlg_symm_toRingHom`. The `le_comap` witness of the tensor-map leg is
obtained from the cheap witness of the transition leg through the ring-hom equality `hring`,
avoiding a whnf explosion over the completed-tensor tower.

signature.text:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.diagXX_transition.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (q : R)
  (hI : I.FG) :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (AlgebraicGeometry.diagChartXX R I q hI)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.bothSummandDiag R I q hI).hom =
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (annulusChartTransitionSpf R I q hI).hom
      (AlgebraicGeometry.diagChartYY R I q hI)

  (hI : I.FG) : AlgebraicGeometry.diagChartYY R I q hI = AlgebraicGeometry.diagChartYY R I q hI

doc:
**Geometric naturality of the diagonal chart.** For an `R`-algebra map `f : A →ₐ[R] A'`, the
diagonal chart intertwines `Spf f` on the base with `mapSpf f f` on the tensor square:
`Spf f ≫ codiagChart_A = codiagChart_{A'} ≫ mapSpf f f`. This is the geometric shadow of
`codiagonal_naturality`, derived purely through `locallyRingedSpaceMap` functoriality.

signature.text:
theorem CompletedTensorProduct.codiagChart_naturality.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {I : Ideal R}
  {A A' : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R A'] [TopologicalSpace A]
  [IsAdicRing (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I)] [TopologicalSpace A']
  [IsAdicRing (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A') I)] (f : A →ₐ[R] A') (hI : I.FG)
  [IsAdicRing (CompletedTensorProduct.idealOfDefinition R I A A)]
  [IsAdicRing (CompletedTensorProduct.idealOfDefinition R I A' A')] :
  CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
      (FormalSpectrum.locallyRingedSpaceMap (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I)
        (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A') I) f.toRingHom ⋯)
      (CompletedTensorProduct.codiagChart hI) =
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CompletedTensorProduct.codiagChart hI)
      (CompletedTensorProduct.mapSpf hI f f)

doc:
Surjectivity of stalk maps is stable under composition: if `g` is surjective on the stalk over
`f x` and `f` is surjective on the stalk over `x`, then so is `f ≫ g`.

signature.text:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_stalkMap_comp.{u_1} {X Y Z : AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace}
  (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : ↑X.toTopCat)
  (hg :
    Function.Surjective
      ⇑(CommRingCat.Hom.hom
          (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.Hom.stalkMap g
            ((CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom f.base) x))))
  (hf :
    Function.Surjective
      ⇑(CommRingCat.Hom.hom (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.Hom.stalkMap f x))) :
  Function.Surjective
    ⇑(CommRingCat.Hom.hom
        (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.Hom.stalkMap (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g)
          x))

doc:
**The diagonal chart is a closed embedding on the preimage.** On each diagonal chart `(b, b)`
of the Tate self-product, the restriction of the underlying map of the glued diagonal `Δ` to the
preimage of the chart is a closed topological embedding. The diagonal is a section of the first
projection `pr₁` (`tateSelfProductDiagonal_comp_pr₁`), so its base map is a global topological
embedding; and via the factorisation `ι b ≫ Δ = diagChart ≫ ι (b,b)` the chart-restricted range is
the closed diagonal locus `range (diagChart.base)`.

signature.text:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.restrictPreimage_diagonal_diagChart.{u, u_1} (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
  (I : Ideal R) (q : R) [IsNoetherianRing R] (hq : q ∈ I) (hI : I.FG) (b : ULift.{u_1, 0} Bool) :
  Topology.IsClosedEmbedding
    ((↑(AlgebraicGeometry.tateSelfProductChartCover R I q hq hI
            { down := (b.down, b.down) })).restrictPreimage
      ⇑(CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom
          (AlgebraicGeometry.tateSelfProductDiagonal R I q hq hI).base))

doc:
**The base map of the per-chart affine diagonal is a closed topological embedding.** The
morphism `diagChart : Spf A ⟶ Spf(A ⊗̂_R A)` is the topology-free `Spf` of the surjective codiagonal
`∇ : A ⊗̂_R A →+* A`, and `Spf` (i.e. `Spec` of the level-`0` reduction) of a surjection is a closed
embedding (`FormalSpectrum.isClosedEmbedding_map_of_surjective`).

doc:
**Descent of a mixed-chart point into the overlap object.** Let `i ≠ j` be two charts of the
four-chart Tate self-product glue datum, let `c : W ⟶ Spf(A ⊗̂_R A)` be a morphism whose composite
with `ι i` absorbs the glue datum's overlap inclusion `f i j ≫ ι i` on ranges (`hf`), and let `t`
satisfy the glue relation `c ≫ ι i = t ≫ c ≫ ι j` (`hglue`).

If a point `z` of the chart `i` has `ι i z` in the range of `diagChart ≫ ι j`, then `z` comes from
a point `v` of `W`, and the transported point `(t ≫ c) v` lies on the affine diagonal.

doc:
**The local-at-target form, uniform in the chart.** On *every* one of the four charts `p` of the
Tate self-product — diagonal and mixed alike — the restriction of `Δ.base` to the preimage of the
chart is a closed topological embedding.

Note the direction of the implication. The per-chart statements
`restrictPreimage_diagonal_diagChart` and `restrictPreimage_diagonal_offDiag` were originally meant
to be glued *into* the global closed embedding; in the end the global statement was proved first
(closedness of `range Δ.base` is what is local-at-target), and the per-chart statements fall out of
it by `Set.restrictPreimage_isClosedEmbedding`. That removes the `(b, b)` / `(b, ¬b)` case split
entirely.

doc:
**The glued diagonal of the Tate curve model is a closed immersion** (EGA I §10.15): its base
map is a closed topological embedding (`isClosedEmbedding_tateSelfProductDiagonal_base`) and all of
its stalk maps are surjective (`tateSelfProductDiagonal_surjective_stalkMap`). Equivalently, the
Tate curve model `𝔈_q` is separated over `Spf R` in the sharp sense, not merely `Mono`.

The statement mirrors the affine `CompletedTensorProduct.diagonal_isClosedImmersion`, which is the
one-chart case: there the closed embedding comes from `Spf` of the surjective codiagonal, here from
the global range computation over the four charts of the self-product.

  (I : Ideal R) (q : R) [IsNoetherianRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsAdicRing I] (hq : q ∈ I)
  (hI : I.FG) :
  Topology.IsClosedEmbedding
      ⇑(CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.hom
          (AlgebraicGeometry.tateSelfProductDiagonal R I q hq hI).base) ∧
    ∀ (y : ↑(AlgebraicGeometry.tateCurveModel R I q hq hI).toTopCat),
      Function.Surjective
        ⇑(CommRingCat.Hom.hom
            (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.Hom.stalkMap
              (AlgebraicGeometry.tateSelfProductDiagonal R I q hq hI) y))

doc:
**The stalk half of the closed immersion, for free from the section identity.** The diagonal is
a section of the first projection (`tateSelfProductDiagonal_comp_pr₁`), and a morphism of locally
ringed spaces with a retraction has surjective stalk maps
(`surjective_stalkMap_of_retraction`): the identity's stalk map factors through it.

This re-proves `tateSelfProductDiagonal_surjective_stalkMap` with no stalk computation and no
reference to the codiagonal — a Tate-level instance of the general fact that separatedness is a
purely topological condition on a split mono.

doc:
**The first-factor overlap of `Spf A ×_{Spf R} Spf A` is affine**: the coproduct
`Spf(A{1/x}^ ⊗̂_R A) ⨿ Spf(A{1/y}^ ⊗̂_R A)` of the two tensored overlap charts is isomorphic to the
single tensored chart `Spf(A{1/(x+y)}^ ⊗̂_R A)`.

This is 671's `tateOverlapChartIso` tensored with a second factor, and it is built the same way:
both sides are open immersions into `Spf C` with the same range
(`range_firstFactorOverlapChart_eq`), so `IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq` supplies the isomorphism
together with the two factorisations below. In particular nothing here needs — or proves — a
splitting of `A{1/(x+y)}^ ⊗̂_R A` as a ring.

    FormalSpectrum.locallyRingedSpaceObj
        (CompletedTensorProduct.idealOfDefinition R I

            (overlapY R I q))

locally ringed spaces agree — their underlying continuous maps by `thickeningMap_base_comp` and
their structure-sheaf components by `thickeningMap_c_comp`, reconciled through the base-map
transport (an `eqToHom` conjugation).

**The `c`-component of the cocone condition**, over a single open `V ⊆ Spf R`: the
level-`(n + 1)` sheaf component of `thickeningMap`, followed by the map on sections induced by the
surjection `R ⧸ I ^ (n + 2) →+* R ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)`, is the level-`n` sheaf component. This is
`thickeningMap_c_comp` read through `thickeningMap_c_app` and the definition of `stepSheafHom`.

The containment proof `h` is deliberately a hypothesis rather than `thickeningOpen_le_comap I n V`:
see the module docstring — supplying it here instead of letting the caller's own proof term be
substituted costs the kernel 11.5 GB.

  {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] {A₁ A₂ : Type u} [CommRing A₁] [CommRing A₂]
  [Algebra R A₁] [Algebra R A₂] (hI : I.FG) {u u' v w : A} {a₁ b₁ : A₁} {a₂ b₂ : A₂}
  (τ₀ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) u ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) v)
  (σ₀ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) (u * u') ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) (w * v))
  (N₁ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) u ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₁) I) a₁)
  (N₁' :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) v ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₂) I) b₂)
  (N₂ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) (u * u') ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₁) I) (a₁ * b₁))
  (N₂' :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) (w * v) ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₂) I) (a₂ * b₂))
  (h₁ : IsUnit ((algebraMap A₁ (Localization.Away (a₁ * b₁))) a₁))
  (h₂ : IsUnit ((algebraMap A₂ (Localization.Away (a₂ * b₂))) b₂))
  (h₃ : IsUnit ((algebraMap A (Localization.Away (u * u'))) u))
  (h₄ : IsUnit ((algebraMap A (Localization.Away (w * v))) v))
  (hfst :
    ∀ (x : FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) u),
      (CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.awayCongrHom I a₁ (a₁ * b₁) hI h₁) (N₁ x) =
        N₂ ((CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.awayCongrHom I u (u * u') hI h₃) x))
  (hsnd :
    ∀ (y : FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) v),
      (CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.awayCongrHom I b₂ (a₂ * b₂) hI h₂) (N₁' y) =
        N₂' ((CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.awayCongrHom I v (w * v) hI h₄) y))
  (hlaw :
    ∀ (y : FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) v),
      σ₀.symm ((CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.furtherLocSnd I w v hI) y) =
        (CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.furtherLocFst I u u' hI) (τ₀.symm y)) :
  (↑(N₂.symm.trans (σ₀.trans N₂')).symm).comp
      (CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.furtherLocSnd I a₂ b₂ hI) =
    (CompletedTensorAwayInterchange.furtherLocFst I a₁ b₁ hI).comp
      ↑(N₁.symm.trans (τ₀.trans N₁')).symm

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.sigma_cocycle_conj.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
  {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] {A₁ A₂ A₃ : Type u} [CommRing A₁] [CommRing A₂]
  [CommRing A₃] [Algebra R A₁] [Algebra R A₂] [Algebra R A₃] {s₁ s₂ s₃ : A} {c₁ : A₁} {c₂ : A₂}
  {c₃ : A₃}
  (σ₁ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₁ ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₂)
  (σ₂ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₂ ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₃)
  (σ₃ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₃ ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₁)
  (M₁ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₁ ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₁) I) c₁)
  (M₂ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₂ ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₂) I) c₂)
  (M₃ :
    FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I) s₃ ≃ₐ[R]
      FormalSpectrum.awayCompletion (Ideal.map (algebraMap R A₃) I) c₃)
  (hc : σ₁.trans (σ₂.trans σ₃) = AlgEquiv.refl) :
  (M₁.symm.trans (σ₁.trans M₂)).trans
      ((M₂.symm.trans (σ₂.trans M₃)).trans (M₃.symm.trans (σ₃.trans M₁))) =
    AlgEquiv.refl

doc:
**Non-vacuity of the fibre-product triple.** At a pairwise distinct triple the geometric
transition `t'` is the derived transition built from `sigma`, not `False.elim`.

signature.text:
theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.datumX_t'_eq.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
  {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (f : ULift.{u, 0} (Fin 3) → A) (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
  [Algebra R B] (hI : I.FG) (i j k : ULift.{u, 0} (Fin 3)) (hij : i ≠ j) (hik : i ≠ k)
  (hjk : j ≠ k) :
  (AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.datumX I f B hI).t' i j k hij hik hjk =
    AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartedFibreDatum.algDataT' hI
      (AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.chartAlgebra I f)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.overlapElt I f)
      (fun i j k x x_1 x_2 => AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.sigma I f hI i j k) i j k hij hik
      hjk

**The glued formal scheme** `X = D(f₀) ∪ D(f₁) ∪ D(f₂) ⊆ Spf A`. Unlike the glued object of
`FormalSchemes.ThreeChartDatum`, this one is an *open subscheme of an affine formal scheme*.

doc:
**The three-chart open-cover datum.** `Spf A` presented by the three basic opens `D(f_i)`,
with chart algebras `A{1/f_i}` and overlaps `D(g_ij) = D(f_i) ∩ D(f_j)`, over the affine base
change `Spf B`. All six geometric triple-overlap fields are derived from `tau` / `sigma` by
`AffineChartedFibreDatumX.ofAlgebraData` and are non-vacuous (see `datumX_xt'_eq`).

fun {R} [CommRing R] I {A} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] f B [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] hI =>
  AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartedFibreDatumX.ofAlgebraData hI
    (AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.chartAlgebra I f)
    (AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.overlapElt I f)
    (fun i j x => AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.tau I f hI i j) ⋯
    (fun i j k x x_1 x_2 => AlgebraicGeometry.ThreeChartCover.sigma I f hI i j k) ⋯ ⋯
